<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF">SUMMARY </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>&#149; Vanguard 500 Index Fund&#146;s
Investor Shares slipped &#150;0.9% in the first half of the fund&#146;s fiscal year,
nearly matching the return of the fund&#146;s target benchmark.<BR> &#149; The fund, like its
benchmark, retreated in the first quarter of 2005 but recovered somewhat in the second
quarter.<BR>&#149; The strong performance of
energy-related stocks was offset by losses in several sectors, including consumer
discretionary and technology. </FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->

<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>CHAIRMAN&#146;S LETTER </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Left-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2> <IMG SRC="picturebrennan.gif" ALIGN="LEFT"> </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Left-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Dear Shareholder,</B> </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>During the six months ended June 30,
2005, Vanguard 500 Index Fund&#146;s Investor Shares returned&#150;0.9% as U.S. stocks
modestly drifted backward and then forward. The Investor Shares&#146; return nearly
matched the &#150;0.8% return of the fund&#146;s benchmark, the Standard &amp; Poor&#146;s
500 Index, and was slightly better than the &#150;1.2% average return of the fund&#146;s
peer group. (The fund&#146;s lower-cost Admiral Shares returned &#150;0.8%, essentially
matching the index&#146;s performance.)</B> </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF">STOCKS MADE LITTLE HEADWAY </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Following a formidable rally to close
out 2004, the U.S. stock market at different times stumbled and recovered during the first
half of 2005, but the net effect was a flat finish for the broad market, as measured by
the Dow Jones Wilshire 5000 Composite Index. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Investors were cheered as home-buying
activity remained high by historical standards, knowing that new homeowners fuel the
economy by buying appliances and other home furnishings. But the market also faced
headwinds: rising short-term interest rates and gas prices (which can curtail consumer
spending), and mounting trade and budget deficits. Some analysts wondered whether even the
home-buying spree was a </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Number Center" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=CENTER><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>1 </FONT></P>
<DIV STYLE="page-break-after:always"></DIV>
<!-- MARKER PAGE="sheet: 3; page: 3" -->
<HR SIZE=5 COLOR=GRAY NOSHADE>



<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>problem, given signs that some buyers
were speculating on real estate. </FONT></P>

<HR SIZE="1" COLOR="Fuchsia" ALIGN="Left">
<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Admiral&#153; Shares </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>A lower-cost class of shares available
to many longtime shareholders and to those with significant investments in the fund. </FONT></P>
<HR SIZE="1" COLOR="Fuchsia" ALIGN="Left">

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Value stocks&#151;those with prices
below average, given the companies&#146; book value and other criteria&#151;prolonged
their five-year roll of outperforming growth stocks, which dominated the market in the
late 1990s. In a reversal of recent trends, returns for large-capitalization stocks topped
those of the market&#146;s smaller companies. International stocks outperformed their U.S.
counterparts; however, a strengthening dollar wiped out most of that edge for U.S.
investors. The dollar rallied as the gap between short-term interest rates in the States
and in Europe widened. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>THE BOND MARKET&#146;S
DICHOTOMY PERSISTED</B> </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The Lehman Brothers Aggregate Bond
Index, which reflects the taxable investment-grade bond market, posted a 2.5% return
during the six months. U.S. government and municipal issues performed best, while
corporate securities matched the index return and mortgage-backed debt trailed. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The Federal Reserve Board raised the
target federal funds rate in four equal steps, leaving it at 3.25% at the end of the
period. The yield of the 3-month U.S. Treasury bill moved in sync, closing the period at
3.12%. Long-term rates didn&#146;t follow, as prices were propped up by demand for the
securities from foreign buyers and pension funds. The yield of the 10-year Treasury note
finished the period at 3.91%, a drop of 31 basis points (0.31 percentage point) over the
six months. The yield of the 30-year Treasury bond fell 64 basis points to 4.19%. </FONT></P>

<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>THE FUND DRIFTED WITHIN A
NARROW RANGE</B> </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Echoing the relatively quiet trading
pattern that the U.S. stock market exhibited during the first half of 2005, the Investor
Shares of Vanguard 500 Index Fund closely tracked the S&amp;P 500 Index with a &#150;2.2%
return during the first quarter, as investors grew cautious. There was a modest turnaround
in market sentiment in the second quarter, and the fund&#146;s Investor Shares advanced
1.3%. The net result was a &#150;0.9% loss for the six-month period. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>As energy supplies continued to be
tight and prices remained high, bullish sentiment continued to dominate trading among
energy-related stocks. The &#147;other energy&#148; sector (+26.0%), which includes firms
engaged in oil and natural gas exploration, production, and related products and services,
recorded the highest gain. Integrated oils (+17.0%) had an even bigger impact on the
fund&#146;s returns because of the larger collective market value of big oil companies
such as ExxonMobil, ConocoPhillips, and Chevron. Other advancing sectors included health
care (+3.5%) and utilities (+3.8%). </FONT></P>

<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Despite these advances, your
fund&#146;s performance, like that of the S&amp;P 500 Index, was hurt by retreats in most
sectors. Concerns about the sustainability of strong consumer spending in the face of
rising short-term interest rates and energy prices weighed down the retail, media, and
entertainment companies that make up the consumer discretionary sector (&#150;5.9%).
Meanwhile, technology companies (&#150;5.2%) declined as corporate IT spending continued
to disappoint. Interest rate trends helped to slow financial services stocks (&#150;2.1%),
the index&#146;s largest sector. And the auto &amp; transportation sector (&#150;15.7%)
continued to struggle with fierce competition and formidable health care and pension
liabilities. </FONT></P>

SUCCESS </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The markets and the news media tend to focus
on what to do <I>now</I>. As we never get tired of reminding our clients, successful
long-term investing doesn&#146;t mean paying attention to yesterday&#146;s performance,
today&#146;s news, or analysts&#146; predictions for tomorrow. Instead, reaching </FONT></P>

<DIV STYLE="page-break-after:always"></DIV>
<!-- MARKER PAGE="sheet: 7; page: 7" -->

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#000000"><B>GLOSSARY OF INVESTMENT
TERMS</B> </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Default" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Beta.</B> </FONT>
<FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">A measure of the magnitude of a fund&#146;s past share-price fluctuations in
relation to the ups and downs of a given market index. The index is assigned a
beta of 1.00. Compared with a given index, a fund with a beta of 1.20 typically
would have seen its share price rise or fall by 12% when the index rose or fell
by 10%. A fund&#146;s beta should be reviewed in conjunction with its R-squared
(see definition below). The lower the R-squared, the less correlation there is
between the fund and the index, and the less reliable beta is as an indicator of
volatility. </FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Earnings Growth Rate.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The
average annual rate of growth in earnings over the past five years for the stocks now in a
fund. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Expense Ratio.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The percentage
of a fund&#146;s average net assets used to pay its annual administrative and advisory
expenses. These expenses directly reduce returns to investors. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Foreign Holdings.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The
percentage of a fund&#146;s equity assets represented by stocks or depositary receipts of
companies based outside the United States. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Median Market Cap.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">An indicator
of the size of companies in which a fund invests; the midpoint of market capitalization
(market price x shares outstanding) of a fund&#146;s stocks, weighted by the proportion of
the fund&#146;s assets invested in each stock. Stocks representing half of the fund&#146;s
assets have market capitalizations above the median, and the rest are below it. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Price/Book Ratio.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The share
price of a stock divided by its net worth, or book value, per share. For a fund, the
weighted average price/book ratio of the stocks it holds. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Price/Earnings Ratio.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The ratio
of a stock&#146;s current price to its per-share earnings over the past year. For a fund,
the weighted average P/E of the stocks it holds. P/E is an indicator of market
expectations about corporate prospects; the higher the P/E, the greater the expectations
for a company&#146;s future growth. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Default" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>R-Squared.</B> </FONT>
<FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">A measure of how much of a fund&#146;s past returns can be explained by the
returns from the market in general, as measured by a given index. If a
fund&#146;s total returns were precisely synchronized with an index&#146;s
returns, its R-squared would be 1.00. If the fund&#146;s returns bore no
relationship to the index&#146;s returns, its R-squared would be 0. </FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Return on Equity.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The annual
average rate of return generated by a company during the past five years for each dollar
of shareholder&#146;s equity (net income divided by shareholder&#146;s equity). For a
fund, the weighted average return on equity for the companies whose stocks it holds. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Short-Term Reserves.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The
percentage of a fund invested in highly liquid, short-term securities that can be readily
converted to cash. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Turnover Rate.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">An indication of
the fund&#146;s trading activity. Funds with high turnover rates incur higher transaction
costs and may be more likely to distribute capital gains (which may be taxable to
investors). The turnover rate excludes in-kind transactions, which have minimal impact on
costs. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Default" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Yield.</B> </FONT>
<FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">A snapshot of a fund&#146;s income from interest and dividends. The yield,
expressed as a percentage of the fund&#146;s net asset value, is based on income
earned over the past 30 days and is annualized, or projected forward for the
coming year. The index yield is based on the current annualized rate of income
provided by securities in the index. </FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Number Center" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=CENTER><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>6 </FONT></P>
<DIV STYLE="page-break-after:always"></DIV>
<!-- MARKER PAGE="sheet: 8; page: 8" -->
<HR SIZE=5 COLOR=GRAY NOSHADE>



<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Sub 2 Left-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2"><B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;PERFORMANCE
SUMMARY</B> </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->

may be achieved by the fund. (For performance data current to the most recent month-end,
which may be\higher or lower than that cited, visit our website at www.vanguard.com.)
Note, too, that both investment returns and principal value can fluctuate widely, so an
investor&#146;s shares, when sold, could be worth more or less than their original cost.
</B>The returns shown do not reflect taxes that a shareholder would pay on fund
distributions or on the sale of fund shares. </FONT></P>

<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>STATEMENT OF NET ASSETS</B> </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>This Statement provides a detailed
list of the fund&#146;s holdings, including each security&#146;s market value on the last
day of the reporting period. Securities are grouped and subtotaled by asset type (common
stocks, bonds, etc.) and by industry sector. Other assets are added to, and liabilities
are subtracted from, the value of <I>Total Investments </I>to calculate the fund&#146;s
<I>Net Assets</I>. Finally, <I>Net Assets </I>are divided by the outstanding shares of the
fund to arrive at its share price, or <I>Net Asset Value (NAV) Per Share</I>. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>At the end of the Statement of Net
Assets, you will find a table displaying the composition of the fund&#146;s net assets.
Because all income and any realized gains must be distributed to shareholders each year,
the bulk of net assets consists of <I>Paid-in Capital </I>(money invested by
shareholders). The amounts shown for <I>Undistributed Net Investment Income </I>and
<I>Accumulated Net Realized Gains </I>usually approximate the sums the fund had available
to distribute to shareholders as income dividends or capital gains as of the statement
date, but may differ because certain investments or transactions may be treated
differently for financial statement and tax purposes. Any <I>Accumulated Net Realized
Losses</I>, and any cumulative excess of distributions over net income or net realized
gains, will appear as negative balances. <I>Unrealized Appreciation (Depreciation) </I>is
the difference between the market value of the fund&#146;s investments and their cost, and
reflects the gains (losses) that would be realized if the fund were to sell all of its
investments at their statement-date values. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The fund provides a complete list of
its holdings four times in each fiscal year, at the quarter-ends. For the second and
fourth fiscal quarters, the lists appear in the fund&#146;s semiannual and annual reports
to shareholders. For the first and third fiscal quarters, the fund files the lists with
the Securities and Exchange Commission on Form N-Q. Shareholders can look up the
fund&#146;s Forms N-Q on the SEC&#146;s website at www.sec.gov. Forms N-Q may also be
reviewed and copied at the SEC&#146;s Public Reference Room (see the back cover of this
report for further information). </FONT></P>

of shares. It also presents the <I>Total Return </I>and shows net investment income and

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF">NOTES TO FINANCIAL
STATEMENTS </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Vanguard 500 Index Fund is registered
under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or mutual
fund. The fund offers two classes of shares, Investor Shares and Admiral Shares. Investor
Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#146;s minimum purchase
requirements. Admiral Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative,
servicing, tenure, and account-size criteria. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>A.</B> </FONT>
<FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted
accounting principles for U.S. mutual funds. The fund consistently follows such
policies in preparing its financial statements. </FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>1.</B>
          <B>Security Valuation: </B>Securities are valued as of the close of trading on
          the New York Stock Exchange (generally 4:00 p.m. Eastern time) on the valuation
          date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official
          closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such
          securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest
          quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not
          readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events
          occurring before the fund&#146;s pricing time but after the close of the
          securities&#146; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of
          trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund
          are valued at that fund&#146;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments
          acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the latest bid prices or
          using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as
          security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by
          independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at
          amortized cost, which approximates market value.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>2.</B>
          <B>Futures Contracts: </B>The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited
          extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market,
          enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The
          fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the
          market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully
          invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for
          liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts
          instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more
          attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with
          the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market
          values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the
          possibility of an illiquid market.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Futures contracts are valued at their
quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate principal amounts of the contracts are not
recorded in the financial statements. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are
recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of
Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when
they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses). </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>3.</B>
          <B>Federal Income Taxes: </B>The fund intends to continue to qualify as a
          regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income.
          Accordingly, no provision for federal income taxes is required in the financial
          statements.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>4.</B>
          <B>Distributions: </B>Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the
          ex-dividend date.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>5.</B>
          <B>Security Lending: </B>The fund may lend its securities to qualified
          institutional borrowers to earn additional income. Security loans are required
          to be secured at all times by collateral at least equal to the market value of
          securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market
          Liquidity Fund, and records a liability for the return of the collateral, during
          the period the securities are on loan. Security lending income represents the
          income earned on investing cash collateral, less expenses associated with the
          loan. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>6.</B> <B>Other: </B>Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend
          date. Interest income includes income distributions received from Vanguard
          Market Liquidity Fund and is accrued daily. Security transactions are accounted
          for on the date securities are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized
          gains (losses) on the sale of investment securities are those of the specific
          securities sold.</FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Each class of shares has equal rights
as to assets and earnings, except that each class separately bears certain class-specific
expenses related to maintenance of shareholder accounts (included in </FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Number Center" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=CENTER><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>19 </FONT></P>

STATEMENTS (CONTINUED) </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Management and Administrative
expenses) and shareholder reporting. Marketing and distribution expenses are allocated to
each class of shares based on a method approved by the board of trustees. Income, other
non-class-specific expenses, and gains and losses on investments are allocated to each
class of shares based on its relative net assets. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>B.</B> </FONT>
<FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The Vanguard Group furnishes at cost investment advisory, corporate
management, administrative, marketing, and distribution services. The costs of
such services are allocated to the fund under methods approved by the board of
trustees. The fund has committed to provide up to 0.40% of its net assets in
capital contributions to Vanguard. At June 30, 2005, the fund had contributed
capital of $13,221,000 to Vanguard (included in Other Assets), representing
0.01% of the fund&#146;s net assets and 13.22% of Vanguard&#146;s
capitalization. The fund&#146;s trustees and officers are also directors and
officers of Vanguard. </FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>C</B> </FONT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2"><B>.
</B>Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net
investment income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes.
Differences may be permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are
reclassified among capital accounts in the financial statements to reflect their
tax character. Temporary differences arise when certain items of income,
expense, gain, or loss are recognized in different periods for financial
statement and tax purposes; these differences will reverse at some time in the
future. Differences in classification may also result from the treatment of
short-term gains as ordinary income for tax purposes. </FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>During the six months ended June 30,
2005, the fund realized $855,077,000 of net capital gains resulting from in-kind
redemptions&#151;in which shareholders exchange fund shares for securities held by the
fund rather than for cash. Because such gains are not taxable to the fund, and are not
distributed to shareholders, they have been reclassified from accumulated net realized
gains to paid-in capital. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The fund&#146;s tax-basis capital
gains and losses are determined only at the end of each fiscal year. For tax purposes, at
December 31, 2004, the fund had available realized losses of $4,432,900,000 to offset
future net capital gains of $193,358,000 through December 31, 2008, $890,248,000 through
December 31, 2009, $3,087,963,000 through December 31, 2010, $145,498,000 through December
31, 2011, $44,874,000 through December 31, 2012, and $70,959,000 through December 31,
2013. The fund will use these capital losses to offset net taxable capital gains, if any,
realized during the year ending December 31, 2005; should the fund realize net capital
losses for the year, the losses will be added to the loss carryforward balances above. </FONT></P>

<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#000000"><B>ABOUT YOUR FUND&#146;S
EXPENSES</B> </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>As a shareholder of the fund, you
incur ongoing costs, which include costs for portfolio management, administrative
services, and shareholder reports (like this one), among others. Operating expenses, which
are deducted from a fund&#146;s gross income, directly reduce the investment return of the
fund. A fund&#146;s expenses are expressed as a percentage of its average net assets. This
figure is known as the expense ratio. The following examples are intended to help you
understand the ongoing costs (in dollars) of investing in your fund and to compare these
costs with those of other mutual funds. The examples are based on an investment of $1,000
made at the beginning of the period shown and held for the entire period. The table below
illustrates your fund&#146;s costs in two ways: </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>&#149;</B> <B>Based on actual fund
return. </B>This section helps you to estimate the actual expenses that you paid over the
period. The &#147;Ending Account Value&#148; shown is derived from the fund&#146;s actual
return, and the third column shows the dollar amount that would have been paid by an
investor who started with $1,000 in the fund. You may use the information here, together
with the amount you invested, to estimate the expenses that you paid over the period. To
do so, simply divide your account value by $1,000 (for example, an $8,600 account value
divided by $1,000 = 8.6), then multiply the result by the number given for your fund under
the heading &#147;Expenses Paid During Period.&#148; </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>&#149;</B> <B>Based on hypothetical
5% yearly return. </B>This section is intended to help you compare your fund&#146;s costs
with those of other mutual funds. It assumes that the fund had a yearly return of 5%
before expenses, but that the expense ratio is unchanged. In this case&#151;because the
return used is not the fund&#146;s actual return&#151;the results do not apply to your
investment. The example is useful in making comparisons because the Securities and
Exchange Commission requires all mutual funds to calculate expenses based on a 5% return.
You can assess your fund&#146;s costs by comparing this hypothetical example with the
hypothetical examples that appear in shareholder reports of other funds. </FONT></P>

applied to your account, your costs would be higher. Your fund does not charge transaction
fees, such as purchase or redemption fees, nor does it carry a &#147;sales load.&#148; The
calculations assume no shares were bought or sold during the period. Your actual costs may
have been higher or lower, depending on the amount of your investment and the timing of
any purchases or redemptions. </FONT></P>

<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2"><B>TRUSTEES RENEW ADVISORY
ARRANGEMENT</B> </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The board of trustees of Vanguard 500
Index Fund has renewed the fund&#146;s investment advisory arrangement with The Vanguard
Group, Inc. Vanguard&#151;through its Quantitative Equity Group&#151;serves as the
investment advisor for the fund. The board determined that continuing the fund&#146;s
internalized management structure was in the best interests of the fund and its
shareholders. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The board based its decision upon its
most recent evaluation of the advisor&#146;s investment staff, portfolio management
process, and performance. The trustees considered the factors discussed below, among
others. However, no single factor determined whether the board approved the arrangement.
Rather, it was the totality of the circumstances that drove the board&#146;s decision. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF">NATURE, EXTENT, AND
QUALITY OF SERVICES </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The board considered the quality of
the fund&#146;s investment management over both short-and long-term periods, and took into
account the organizational depth and stability of the advisor. Vanguard has been managing
investments for more than two decades. George U. Sauter, Vanguard managing director and
chief investment officer, has been in the investment management business since 1985 and
oversees more than $600 billion in assets (stocks and bonds). Mr. Sauter has led the
Quantitative Equity Group since 1987. The Quantitative Equity Group adheres to a sound,
disciplined investment management process; the team has considerable experience,
stability, and depth. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The board concluded that
Vanguard&#146;s experience, stability, depth, and performance, among other factors,
warranted continuation of the advisory arrangement. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF">INVESTMENT PERFORMANCE </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The board considered the short- and
long-term performance of the fund, including any periods of outperformance or
underperformance of its relevant benchmark and peer group. The board noted that the fund
has performed in line with expectations, and that its results have been consistent with
its investment strategies. Information about the fund&#146;s performance, including some
of the data considered by the board, can be found in the &#147;Performance Summary&#148;
section of this report. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF">COST </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The fund&#146;s expense ratio was far
below the average expense ratio charged by funds in its peer group. The fund&#146;s
advisory expense ratio was also well below its peer-group average. Information about the
fund&#146;s expense ratio appears in the &#147;About Your Fund&#146;s Expenses&#148;
section of this report as well as in the &#147;Financial Statements&#148; section. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The board does not conduct a
profitability analysis of Vanguard because of Vanguard&#146;s unique &#147;at-cost&#148;
structure. Unlike most other mutual fund management companies, Vanguard is owned by the
funds it oversees, and produces &#147;profits&#148; only in the form of reduced expenses
for fund shareholders. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF">THE BENEFIT OF ECONOMIES
OF SCALE </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The board of trustees concluded that
Vanguard 500 Index Fund&#146;s low-cost arrangement with Vanguard ensures that the fund
will realize economies of scale as it grows, with the cost to shareholders declining as
fund assets increase. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The board will consider whether to
renew the advisory arrangement again after a one-year period. </FONT></P>

<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>CHAIRMAN&#146;S LETTER </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Left-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF">Dear Shareholder, </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF">During the first six months of 2005,
U.S. stock prices advanced very little, if at all. The Investor Shares of Vanguard
Small-Cap Index Fund, Small-Cap Growth Index Fund, and Small-Cap Value Index Fund posted
returns of 0.9%, 0.0%, and 1.7%, respectively. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>STOCKS MADE LITTLE HEADWAY</B> </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Following a formidable rally to close
out 2004, U.S. stocks at different times stumbled and surged during the first half of
2005, but the net effect was a flat finish for the broad market, as measured by the Dow
Jones Wilshire 5000 Composite Index. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Number Center" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=CENTER><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2> 1 </FONT></P>
<DIV STYLE="page-break-after:always"></DIV>
<!-- MARKER PAGE="sheet: 3; page: 3" -->
<HR SIZE=5 COLOR=GRAY NOSHADE>



<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Investors were cheered as home-buying
activity remained high, knowing that new homeowners fuel the economy by buying appliances
and other home furnishings. But the market also faced crosscurrents: rising short-term
interest rates and gas prices (which can curtail consumer spending); slower corporate
profit growth; and mounting trade and budget deficits. Some analysts wondered if even the
home-buying spree was a problem, given signs that some buyers were speculating on real
estate. </FONT></P>

<HR COLOR="Fuchsia" ALIGN="Left">
<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->

<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Value stocks&#151;those with prices
below average, given the companies&#146; book value and other criteria&#151;prolonged
their five-year roll of outperforming growth stocks, which dominated the market in the
late 1990s. According to indexes maintained by Frank Russell Company, returns for
large-capitalization stocks topped those of the market&#146;s smaller companies, a
reversal of recent trends. But according to Morgan Stanley Capital International, whose
indexes the Vanguard small-cap index funds track, smaller shares did better. International
stocks outperformed their U.S. counterparts; however, a strengthening dollar wiped out
most of that edge for U.S. investors. The dollar rallied as the gap between short-term
interest rates in the United States and in Europe widened. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The Federal Reserve Board raised the
target federal funds rate in four equal steps, leaving it at 3.25% at the end of the
period. The yield of the 3-month U.S. Treasury bill moved in sync, closing the period at
3.12%. Long-term rates didn&#146;t follow, as bond prices were propped up by demand for
the securities from foreign buyers and pension funds. The yield of the 10-year Treasury
note finished the period at 3.91%, a drop of 31 basis points (0.31 percentage point) over
the six months. The yield of the 30-year Treasury bond fell 64 basis points to 4.19%. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>SMALLER STOCKS RECORDED
ONLY MODEST GAINS</B> </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Two years of exceptional returns for
small-cap stocks came to a halt during the first half of 2005, and, at least according to
the MSCI indexes, the underperformance of larger stocks narrowed significantly. Two of the
three small-cap index funds delivered positive returns for shareholders; the third
finished essentially flat. As is typically the case, the Small-Cap Index Fund, which
includes growth and value stocks, posted a return that was roughly midway between the
returns of the two style-based portfolios. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Within the three small-cap index
funds, most industry sectors saw only modest gains. Most of the Small-Cap Index
Fund&#146;s half-year returns (+0.9% for Investor Shares) came from solid </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Number Center" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=CENTER><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>3 </FONT></P>
<DIV STYLE="page-break-after:always"></DIV>
<!-- MARKER PAGE="sheet: 5; page: 5" -->
<HR SIZE=5 COLOR=GRAY NOSHADE>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>contributions in three sectors:
consumer discretionary, utilities, and &#147;other energy.&#148; However, financial
services and technology issues, which together made up about one-third of the target
index, turned in poor results. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Within the Small-Cap Growth Index
Fund, sector performance was very similar to that of the Small-Cap Index Fund, with
utilities shares, consumer discretionary issues, and &#147;other energy&#148;
stocks&#151;largely exploration, production, and service-related companies&#151;among the
top performers. Health care stocks&#151;which accounted for roughly 20% of the fund&#146;s
holdings&#151;made only a modest contribution to overall return. Technology and financial
services stocks were the fund&#146;s largest detractors. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The Small-Cap Value Index Fund&#146;s
returns (+1.7% for Investor Shares) topped those of the fund&#146;s growth-oriented
sibling. The fund saw strong contributions from the utilities and &#147;other energy&#148;
sectors. Financial services stocks, the largest sector in the index, provided modest
returns that helped to buoy the fund during the period. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>DIVERSIFICATION REMAINS
KEY TO LONG-TERM SUCCESS</B> </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The last several years provide an
object lesson to investors about the enduring value of diversification. For example,
throughout much of the 1990s, when U.S. stocks were booming, it was difficult to persuade
some investors to diversify their portfolios with either bonds or international stocks.
Then domestic stocks tumbled during the 2000&#150;2002 bear market, and bonds excelled.
Such asynchronous ups and downs suggest that, over time, a prudent strategy is to be well
diversified across asset classes. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Investors enhance their ability to
meet their long-term goals by sticking with a program balanced among stock, bond, and
money market investments in proportions that fit their goals, time horizon, and tolerance
for risk. At Vanguard, we believe that staying faithful to such a strategy&#151;rather
than listening to the &#147;noise&#148; created by short-term market
fluctuations&#151;will give you the best chance of reaching your financial goals. If you
continue to adhere to these </FONT></P>

<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>GLOSSARY OF INVESTMENT
TERMS </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Default" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Beta.</B> </FONT>
<FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">A measure of the magnitude of a fund&#146;s past share-price fluctuations in
relation to the ups and downs of a given market index. The index is assigned a
beta of 1.00. Compared with a given index, a fund with a beta of 1.20 typically
would have seen its share price rise or fall by 12% when the index rose or fell
by 10%. A fund&#146;s beta should be reviewed in conjunction with its R-squared
(see definition below). The lower the R-squared, the less correlation there is
between the fund and the index, and the less reliable beta is as an indicator of
volatility. </FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Earnings Growth Rate.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The
average annual rate of growth in earnings over the past five years for the stocks now in a
fund. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Expense Ratio.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The percentage
of a fund&#146;s average net assets used to pay its annual administrative and advisory
expenses. These expenses directly reduce returns to investors. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Foreign Holdings.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The
percentage of a fund&#146;s equity assets represented by stocks or depositary receipts of
companies based outside the United States. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Median Market Cap.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">An indicator
of the size of companies in which a fund invests; the midpoint of market capitalization
(market price x shares outstanding) of a fund&#146;s stocks, weighted by the proportion of
the fund&#146;s assets invested in each stock. Stocks representing half of the fund&#146;s
assets have market capitalizations above the median, and the rest are below it. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Price/Book Ratio.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The share
price of a stock divided by its net worth, or book value, per share. For a fund, the
weighted average price/book ratio of the stocks it holds. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Price/Earnings Ratio.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The ratio
of a stock&#146;s current price to its per-share earnings over the past year. For a fund,
the weighted average P/E of the stocks it holds. P/E is an indicator of market
expectations about corporate prospects; the higher the P/E, the greater the expectations
for a company&#146;s future growth. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Default" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>R-Squared.</B> </FONT>
<FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">A measure of how much of a fund&#146;s past returns can be explained by the
returns from the market in general, as measured by a given index. If a
fund&#146;s total returns were precisely synchronized with an index&#146;s
returns, its R-squared would be 1.00. If the fund&#146;s returns bore no
relationship to the index&#146;s returns, its R-squared would be 0. </FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Return on Equity.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The annual
average rate of return generated by a company during the past five years for each dollar
of shareholder&#146;s equity (net income divided by shareholder&#146;s equity). For a
fund, the weighted average return on equity for the companies whose stocks it holds. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Short-Term Reserves.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The
percentage of a fund invested in highly liquid, short-term securities that can be readily
converted to cash. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Turnover Rate.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">An indication of
the fund&#146;s trading activity. Funds with high turnover rates incur higher transaction
costs and may be more likely to distribute capital gains (which may be taxable to
investors). The turnover rate excludes in-kind transactions, which have minimal impact on
costs. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Yield.</B> </FONT>
<FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">A snapshot of a fund&#146;s income from interest and dividends. The yield,
expressed as a percentage of the fund&#146;s net asset value, is based on income
earned over the past 30 days and is annualized, or projected forward for the
coming year. The index yield is based on the current annualized rate of income
provided by securities in the index. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF">STATEMENT OF NET
ASSETS&#151;INVESTMENTS SUMMARY </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>This Statement summarizes each
fund&#146;s holdings by asset type (common stocks, bonds, etc.) and by industry sector.
Details are reported for each of the fund&#146;s 50 largest individual holdings and for
investments that, in total for any issuer, represent more than 1% of the fund&#146;s
<I>Net Assets</I>. The total value of smaller holdings is reported as a single amount
within each category. Other assets are added to, and liabilities are subtracted from, the
value of <I>Total Investments </I>to calculate the fund&#146;s <I>Net Assets</I>. Finally,
<I>Net Assets </I>are divided by the outstanding shares of the fund to arrive at its share
price, or <I>Net Asset Value (NAV) Per Share</I>. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>At the end of the Statement you will
find a table displaying the composition of the fund&#146;s net assets. Because all income
and any realized gains must be distributed to shareholders each year, the bulk of net
assets consists of <I>Paid-in Capital </I>(money invested by shareholders). The amounts
shown for <I>Undistributed Net Investment Income </I>and <I>Accumulated Net Realized Gains
</I>usually approximate the sums the fund had available to distribute to shareholders as
income dividends or capital gains as of the statement date, but may differ because certain
investments or transactions may be treated differently for financial statement and tax
purposes. Any <I>Accumulated Net Realized Losses</I>, and any cumulative excess of
distributions over net income or net realized gains, will appear as negative balances.
<I>Unrealized Appreciation (Depreciation) </I>is the difference between the market value
of the fund&#146;s investments and their cost, and reflects the gains (losses) that would
be realized if the fund were to sell all of its investments at their statement-date
values. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Each fund provides a complete list of
its holdings four times in each fiscal year, at the quarter-ends. For the second and
fourth fiscal quarters, the complete listing of the fund&#146;s holdings is available
electronically on Vanguard.com and on the Securities and Exchange Commission&#146;s
website (www.sec.gov), or you can have it mailed to you without charge by calling
800-662-7447. For the first and third fiscal quarters, the fund files the lists with the
SEC on Form N-Q. Shareholders can look up the fund&#146;s Forms N-Q on the SEC&#146;s
website; Forms N-Q may also be reviewed and copied at the SEC&#146;s Public Reference Room
(see the back cover of this report for further information). </FONT></P>

<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>NOTES TO FINANCIAL
STATEMENTS</B> </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Vanguard Small-Cap Index, Small-Cap Growth
Index, and Small-Cap Value Index Funds are registered under the Investment Company Act of
1940 as open-end investment companies, or mutual funds. The Small-Cap Index Fund offers
four classes of shares: Investor Shares, Admiral Shares, Institutional Shares, and VIPER
Shares. The Small-Cap Growth Index and Small-Cap Value Index Funds each offer three
classes of shares, Investor Shares, Institutional Shares, and VIPER Shares. Investor
Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#146;s minimum purchase
requirements. Admiral Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative,
servicing, tenure, and account-size criteria. Institutional Shares are designed for
investors who meet certain administrative and servicing criteria and invest a minimum of
$5 million. VIPER Shares are listed for trading on the American Stock Exchange; they can
be purchased and sold through a broker. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>A.</B> </FONT>
<FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted
accounting principles for U.S. mutual funds. The funds consistently follow such
policies in preparing their financial statements. </FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>1.</B>
          <B>Security Valuation: </B>Securities are valued as of the close of trading on
          the New York Stock Exchange (generally 4:00 p.m., Eastern time) on the valuation
          date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official
          closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such
          securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest
          quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not
          readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events
          occurring before the fund&#146;s pricing time but after the close of the
          securities&#146; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of
          trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund
          are valued at that fund&#146;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments
          acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the latest bid prices or
          using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as
          security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by
          independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at
          amortized cost, which approximates market value.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>2.</B>
          <B>Futures Contracts: </B>The funds use index futures contracts to a limited
          extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market,
          enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. A
          fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the
          market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully
          invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for
          liquidity. A fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead
          of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more
          attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with
          the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market
          values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the
          possibility of an illiquid market.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Futures contracts are valued at their
quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate principal amounts of the contracts are not
recorded in the financial statements. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are
recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of
Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when
they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses). </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>3.</B>
          <B>Federal Income Taxes: </B>Each fund intends to continue to qualify as a
          regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income.
          Accordingly, no provision for federal income taxes is required in the financial
          statements.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>4.</B>
          <B>Distributions: </B>Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the
          ex-dividend date.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Default" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>5.</B>
          <B>Security Lending: </B>The funds may lend their securities to qualified
          institutional borrowers in order to earn additional income. Security loans are
          required to be secured at all times by collateral at least equal to the market
          value of securities loaned. The funds invest cash collateral received in
          Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund, and record a liability for the return of the
          collateral, during the period the securities are on loan. Security lending
          income represents the income earned on investing cash collateral, less expenses
          associated with the loan.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Number Center" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=CENTER><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>37 </FONT></P>

<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="1" COLOR="#FF00FF">NOTES TO FINANCIAL
STATEMENTS (CONTINUED) </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>6.</B>
          <B>Other: </B>Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest
          income includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity
          Fund and is accrued daily. Security transactions are accounted for on the date
          securities are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses)
          on the sale of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.
          Each class of shares has equal rights as to assets and earnings, except that
          each class separately bears certain class-specific expenses related to
          maintenance of shareholder accounts (included in Management and Administrative
          expenses) and shareholder reporting. Marketing and distribution expenses are
          allocated to each class of shares based on a method approved by the board of
          trustees. Income, other non-class-specific expenses, and gains and losses on
          investments are allocated to each class of shares based on its relative net
          assets.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Default" -->

     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>C.</B> </FONT>
<FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net
investment income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes.
Differences may be permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are
reclassified among capital accounts in the financial statements to reflect their
tax character. Temporary differences arise when certain items of income,
expense, gain, or loss are recognized in different periods for financial
statement and tax purposes; these differences will reverse at some time in the
future. Differences in classification may also result from the treatment of
short-term gains as ordinary income for tax purposes. </FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>During the six months ended June 30,
2005, the Small-Cap Index and Small-Cap Growth Index Funds realized $115,352,000 and
$5,929,000, respectively, of net capital gains resulting from in-kind redemptions&#151;in
which shareholders exchanged fund shares for securities held by the fund rather than for
cash. Because such gains are not taxable to the funds, and are not distributed to
shareholders, they have been reclassified from accumulated net realized gains to paid-in
capital. </FONT></P>

<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>ABOUT YOUR FUND&#146;S
EXPENSES </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>As a shareholder of the fund, you
incur ongoing costs, which include costs for portfolio management, administrative
services, and shareholder reports (like this one), among others. Operating expenses, which
are deducted from a fund&#146;s gross income, directly reduce the investment return of the
fund. A fund&#146;s expenses are expressed as a percentage of its average net assets. This
figure is known as the expense ratio. The following examples are intended to help you
understand the ongoing costs (in dollars) of investing in your fund and to compare these
costs with those of other mutual funds. The examples are based on an investment of $1,000
made at the beginning of the period shown and held for the entire period. </FONT></P>






<TABLE CELLPADDING=0 CELLSPACING=0 BORDER=0 WIDTH=90%>
<TR>
     <TD COLSPAN=4><HR NOSHADE COLOR=#000000 SIZE=1></TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN=Bottom>
     <TH ALIGN="Left" COLSPAN="2"><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Six Months Ended June 30, 2005</FONT></TH>

     <TH><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2></FONT></TH>

simply divide your account value by $1,000 (for example, an $8,600 account value divided

heading &#147;Expenses Paid During Period.&#148; </FONT></P>

hypothetical examples that appear in shareholder reports of other funds. </FONT></P>

<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>TRUSTEES RENEW ADVISORY
ARRANGEMENT </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The board of trustees of Vanguard
Small-Cap Index Fund, Small-Cap Growth Index Fund, and Small-Cap Value Index Fund has
renewed the funds&#146; investment advisory arrangement with The Vanguard Group, Inc.
Vanguard&#151;through its Quantitative Equity Group&#151;serves as the investment advisor
for the funds. The board determined that continuing the funds&#146; internalized
management structure was in the best interests of the funds and their shareholders. The
board based its decision upon its most recent evaluation of the advisor&#146;s investment
staff, portfolio management process, and performance. The trustees considered the factors
discussed below, among others. However, no single factor determined whether the board
approved the arrangement. Rather, it was the totality of the circumstances that drove the
board&#146;s decision. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF">NATURE, EXTENT, AND
QUALITY OF SERVICES </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The board considered the quality of
the funds&#146; investment management over both short-and long-term periods, and took into
account the organizational depth and stability of the advisor. Vanguard has been managing
investments for more than two decades. George U. Sauter, Vanguard managing director and
chief investment officer, has been in the investment management business since 1985 and
oversees more than $600 billion in assets (stocks and bonds). Mr. Sauter has led the
Quantitative Equity Group since 1987. The Quantitative Equity Group adheres to a sound,
disciplined investment management process; the team has considerable experience,
stability, and depth. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The board concluded that
Vanguard&#146;s experience, stability, depth, and performance, among other factors,
warranted continuation of the advisory arrangement. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF">INVESTMENT PERFORMANCE </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The board considered the short- and
long-term performance of the funds, including any periods of outperformance or
underperformance of relevant benchmarks and peer groups. The board noted that the funds
have performed in line with expectations, and that their results have been consistent with
their investment strategies. Information about the funds&#146; performance, including some
of the data considered by the board, can be found in the &#147;Performance Summaries&#148;
section of this report. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF">COST </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The funds&#146; expense ratios were
far below the average expense ratios charged by funds in their respective peer groups. The
funds&#146; advisory expense ratios were also well below their peer-group averages.
Information about the funds&#146; expense ratios appears in the &#147;About Your
Fund&#146;s Expenses&#148; section of this report as well as in the &#147;Financial
Statements&#148; section. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The board does not conduct a
profitability analysis of Vanguard because of Vanguard&#146;s unique &#147;at-cost&#148;
structure. Unlike most other mutual fund management companies, Vanguard is owned by the
funds it oversees, and produces &#147;profits&#148; only in the form of reduced expenses
for fund shareholders. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF">THE BENEFIT OF ECONOMIES
OF SCALE </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The board of trustees concluded that
the funds&#146; low-cost arrangement with Vanguard ensures that the funds will realize
economies of scale as they grow, with the cost to shareholders declining as fund assets
increase. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The board will consider whether to
renew the advisory arrangement again after a one-year period. </FONT></P>

<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>INVEST WITH VANGUARD FOR
YOUR RE TIREMENT </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Vanguard offers low-cost, high-quality
solutions that combine a variety of investment choices to help you achieve your retirement
goals. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>A <B>Vanguard traditional IRA
</B>enables you to make deductible or nondeductible contributions that can grow
tax-deferred until you take distributions in retirement, while a <B>Vanguard Roth IRA
</B>allows you to make nondeductible contributions with tax-free withdrawals when you take
qualified distributions. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>With either type of Vanguard IRA&reg;,
your investment options include: </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>&#149; Vanguard mutual
funds </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Select from our comprehensive lineup
of more than 70 low-cost mutual funds suitable for retirement investing&#151;all with no
sales commissions&#151;to help you reach your retirement goals. We offer a broad selection
of stock, bond, balanced, and money market funds. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>&#149; Vanguard Target
Retirement Funds </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Choose a single, all-in-one portfolio
that is professionally managed and well diversified. It automatically shifts from a more
aggressive to a more conservative asset allocation as your target retirement date
approaches, so you can leave the time-consuming details of portfolio management to
Vanguard. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>&#149; Other investment
options </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Consolidate and build your portfolio
in a single account that provides access to the universe of stocks, bonds, options,
certificates of deposit (CDs), exchange-traded funds (ETFs), and non-Vanguard mutual funds
through Vanguard Brokerage Services&reg;. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
