<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>MAXIMIZE YOUR RETIREMENT
INVESTMENTS </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Are you taking full advantage of your
IRA? You should be. With increased contribution limits, these tax-advantaged accounts are
powerful options for retirement savers. To take full advantage of your retirement account,
consider these simple, but important, steps: </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>&#149; <B>Contribute the maximum
amount each year.</B> </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>If you invest as much in your IRA as
the law allows&#151;$4,000 for 2005 if you are under the age of 50, and $4,500 if you are
aged 50 or older&#151;you will increase your chances of meeting your retirement goals.
Provided you meet the eligibility requirements, max out your contribution every year you
can. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>&#149; Make automatic
contributions. </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>You can make regular contributions to
your IRA by taking advantage of Vanguard&#146;s Automatic Investment Plan, which deducts
your contributions from your bank account on a schedule you select&#151;making retirement
investing a healthy habit. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>&#149; Keep your savings
on course. </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Unless you&#146;ve invested in a
Vanguard Target Retirement Fund, you should rebalance your account periodically to ensure
that your target asset allocations are aligned to meet your retirement objectives. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>&#149; Protect those you
care about. </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>You determine who will receive your
retirement assets after your death, so it&#146;s important to keep your beneficiary
designations up to date. They will generally override any other instructions&#151;even
those in your will. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>&#149; Adopt a long-term
approach. </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>A successful investment strategy
requires a long-term perspective and staying on course&#151;even when the financial
markets are declining. Market-timing and performance-chasing are losing strategies that
can cause you to stray from the path to your retirement goals. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->

benchmark, which incorporates many construction methodologies endorsed by Vanguard, is not expected to cause any adverse tax consequences for the shareholders.</FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Left-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="1" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>STOCKS MADE LITTLE HEADWAY</B> </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P STYLE="margin-left:5%; margin-right:30%;"><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Following a formidable rally to close out 2004, U.S. stocks at different times stumbled and surged during the first half of 2005, but the net effect was a flat finish for the broad market, as measured by the
Dow Jones Wilshire 5000 Composite Index.</FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P STYLE="margin-left:5%; margin-right:30%;"><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Investors were cheered as home-buying activity remained high, knowing that new homeowners fuel the economy by buying appliances and other home furnishings. But the market also faced crosscurrents: rising
short-term interest rates and gas prices (which can curtail consumer spending); and mounting trade and budget deficits. Some analysts wondered if even the home-buying spree was a problem, given the rising
proportion of buyers who are speculating on real estate.</FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P STYLE="margin-left:5%; margin-right:30%;"><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Value stocks-those with prices below average, given the companies' book value and other criteria--prolonged their five-year roll of outperforming growth stocks, which dominated the market in the late 1990s.
In a reversal of recent trends, returns for large-capitalization stocks topped those of the market's smaller companies. International stocks outperformed their U.S. counterparts; however, a strengthening
dollar wiped out most of that edge for U.S. investors. The dollar rallied as the gap between short-term interest rates in the States and in Europe widened.</FONT></P>

<P ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="1" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>THE BOND MARKET&#146;S
DICHOTOMY PERSISTED </b></FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P STYLE="margin-left:5%; margin-right:30%;"><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>
The
Lehman Brothers Aggregate Bond Index, which reflects the performance of the taxable
investment-grade bond market, gained 2.5% during the six months. U.S. government and
municipal issues performed best, while corporate securities matched the index return and
mortgage-backed debt trailed.</FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P STYLE="margin-left:5%; margin-right:30%;"><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>
The
Federal Reserve Board raised the target federal funds rate in four equal steps, leaving it
at 3.25% at the end of the period. The yield of the 3-month U.S. Treasury bill moved in
sync, closing the period at 3.12%. Long-term rates refused to follow, their prices propped
up by demand for the securities from foreign buyers and pension funds. The yield of the
10-year Treasury note finished the period at 3.91%, a drop of 31 basis points (0.31
percentage point) over the six months. The yield of the 30-year Treasury bond fell 64
basis points to 4.19%.</FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Left-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="1" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>THE FUNDS PRODUCED GAINS
IN A CHALLENGING PERIOD</b> </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P STYLE="margin-left:5%; margin-right:30%;"><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>
The
six-month results for both funds were reasonably good, considering that the first half of
2005 was generally a fallow period for stocks. The 2.0% return of the Extended Market
Index Fund&#146;s Investor Shares matched that of its chain-linked target, and the 4.0%
return of the Mid-Cap Index Fund&#146;s Investor Shares slightly bested the 3.9% return of
the Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI) US Mid Cap 450 Index.</FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P STYLE="margin-left:5%; margin-right:30%;"><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>
The
Extended Market Index Fund benefited from positive returns in 8 of its 12 industry
sectors. The strongest results came from the health care, utilities, and &#147;other
energy&#148; sectors, the last of which consists of companies that provide exploration,
research, and other services to oil drillers. The &#147;other energy&#148; group had a
six-month return of almost 23%, and alone accounted for more than half of the fund&#146;s
2.0% return. The fund&#146;s holdings in the economically sensitive financial services
sector (its largest industry group) </FONT></P>

prices and global demand. As was the case for the Extended Market Index Fund, the

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P STYLE="margin-left:5%; margin-right:30%;"><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>
The
markets and the news media tend to focus on what to do now. As we never get tired of
reminding Vanguard&#146;s clients, successful long-term investing doesn&#146;t mean paying
attention to yesterday&#146;s performance, today&#146;s news, or analysts&#146;
predictions for tomorrow. Instead, reaching your long-term goals requires a more patient
approach.</FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P STYLE="margin-left:5%; margin-right:30%;"><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>
Whether
the stock market rises or falls sharply or, as in the past six months, meanders sideways,
long-term success is much more likely when you ignore the daily noise of the marketplace
and maintain a steady, diversified mix of low-cost stock, bond, and short-term investments
tailored to your circumstances. I hope you take advantage of our website, Vanguard.com,
where you&#146;ll find extensive information and useful tools to help you apply these
principles to your own portfolio.</FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Default" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Beta.</B> </FONT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2"><B>&nbsp;
</B>A measure of the magnitude of a fund&#146;s past share-price fluctuations in
relation to the ups and downs of a given market index. The index is assigned a
beta of 1.00. Compared with a given index, a fund with a beta of 1.20 typically
would have seen its share price rise or fall by 12% when the index rose or fell
by 10%. A fund&#146;s beta should be reviewed in conjunction with its R-squared
(see definition below). The lower the R-squared, the less correlation there is
between the fund and the index, and the less reliable beta is as an indicator of
volatility. </FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Earnings Growth Rate.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The
average annual rate of growth in earnings over the past five years for the stocks now in a
fund. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Expense Ratio.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The percentage
of a fund&#146;s average net assets used to pay its annual administrative and advisory
expenses. These expenses directly reduce returns to investors. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Foreign Holdings.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The
percentage of a fund&#146;s equity assets represented by stocks or depositary receipts of
companies based outside the United States. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Median Market Cap.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">An indicator
of the size of companies in which a fund invests; the midpoint of market capitalization
(market price x shares outstanding) of a fund&#146;s stocks, weighted by the proportion of
the fund&#146;s assets invested in each stock. Stocks representing half of the fund&#146;s
assets have market capitalizations above the median, and the rest are below it. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Price/Book Ratio.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The share
price of a stock divided by its net worth, or book value, per share. For a fund, the
weighted average price/book ratio of the stocks it holds. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Price/Earnings Ratio.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The ratio
of a stock&#146;s current price to its per-share earnings over the past year. For a fund,
the weighted average P/E of the stocks it holds. P/E is an indicator of market
expectations about corporate prospects; the higher the P/E, the greater the expectations
for a company&#146;s future growth. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Default" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>R-Squared.</B> </FONT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2"><B>&nbsp;
</B>A measure of how much of a fund&#146;s past returns can be explained by the
returns from the market in general, as measured by a given index. If a
fund&#146;s total returns were precisely synchronized with an index&#146;s
returns, its R-squared would be 1.00. If the fund&#146;s returns bore no
relationship to the index&#146;s returns, its R-squared would be 0. </FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Return on Equity.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The annual
average rate of return generated by a company during the past five years for each dollar
of shareholder&#146;s equity (net income divided by shareholder&#146;s equity). For a
fund, the weighted average return on equity for the companies whose stocks it holds. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Short-Term Reserves.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The
percentage of a fund invested in highly liquid, short-term securities that can be readily
converted to cash. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Turnover Rate.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">An indication of
the fund&#146;s trading activity. Funds with high turnover rates incur higher transaction
costs and may be more likely to distribute capital gains (which may be taxable to
investors). The turnover rate excludes in-kind transactions, which have minimal impact on
costs. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Default" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Yield.</B> </FONT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2"><B>&nbsp;
</B>A snapshot of a fund&#146;s income from interest and dividends. The yield,
expressed as a percentage of the fund&#146;s net asset value, is based on income
earned over the past 30 days and is annualized, or projected forward for the
coming year. The index yield is based on the current annualized rate of income
provided by securities in the index. </FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Rule Single" FSL="Default" -->
     <HR ALIGN=LEFT WIDTH=100% SIZE=1 NOSHADE>

<P>
<FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The Statement of Net Assets-an  integral part of the Financial  Statements for the Vanguard Extended Market Index Fund--is included as an insert to this report. The Mid-Cap Index Fund's Statement of Net Assets
is provided below.</FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="1" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>STATEMENT OF NET ASSETS</B> </FONT> </H1>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P>
<FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">This Statement provides a detailed list of the fund's holdings, including each security's
market value on the last day of the reporting period. Securities are grouped and subtotaled by asset type (common
stocks, bonds, etc.) and by industry sector. Other assets are added to, and liabilities are subtracted from, the value of <I>Total
Investments </I>to calculate the fund's <I>Net Assets</I>. Finally, <I>Net Assets </I>are divided
by the outstanding shares of the fund to arrive at its share price, or <I>Net Asset Value (NAV) </I>Per Share.
<br><br>
At the end of the Statement of Net Assets, you will find a table displaying the composition of the fund's net assets. Because all
income and any realized gains must be distributed to shareholders each year,
the bulk of net assets consists of <I>Paid-in Capital </I>(money invested by shareholders). The amounts shown for <I>Undistributed Net Investment Income
</I>and <I>Accumulated Net Realized Gains </I>usually approximate the sums
the fund had available to distribute to shareholders as income dividends or capital gains as of the statement date, but may differ because
certain investments or transactions may be treated differently for
financial statement and tax purposes. Any <I>Accumulated Net Realized Losses</I>, and any cumulative excess of distributions over net income
or net realized gains, will appear as negative balances. <I>Unrealized
Appreciation (Depreciation) </I>is the difference between the market value of the fund's investments and their cost, and reflects the
gains (losses) that would be realized if the fund were to sell all of its
investments at their statement-date values.
<br><br>
The fund provides a complete list of its holdings four times in each fiscal year, at the quarter-ends. For the second and fourth fiscal
quarters, the lists appear in the fund's semiannual and annual reports
to shareholders. For the first and third fiscal quarters, the fund files the lists with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Form N-Q.
Shareholders can look up the fund's Forms N-Q on the SEC's website
at www.sec.gov. Forms N-Q may also be reviewed and copied at the SEC's Public Reference Room (see the back cover of this report for further
information). </FONT> </P>

<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>This table summarizes each fund&#146;s
investment results and distributions to shareholders on a per-share basis for each class
of shares. It also presents the <I>Total Return </I>and shows net investment income and
expenses as percentages of average net assets. These data will help you assess: the
variability of the fund&#146;s net income and total returns from year to year; the
relative contributions of net income and capital gains to the fund&#146;s total return;
how much it costs to operate the fund; and the extent to which the fund tends to
distribute capital gains. The table also shows the <I>Portfolio Turnover Rate</I>, a
measure of trading activity. A turnover rate of 100% means that the average security is
held in the fund for one year. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="1" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>NOTES TO FINANCIAL
STATEMENTS</B> </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Vanguard Extended Market Index and
Mid-Cap Index Funds are registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as open-end
investment companies, or mutual funds. Both funds offer four classes of shares: Investor
Shares, Admiral Shares, Institutional Shares, and VIPER Shares. Investor Shares are
available to any investor who meets the fund&#146;s minimum purchase requirements. Admiral
Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative, servicing, tenure, and
account-size criteria. Institutional Shares are designed for investors who meet certain
administrative and servicing criteria and invest a minimum of $5 million. VIPER Shares are
listed for trading on the American Stock Exchange; they can be purchased and sold through
a broker. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Hang Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <TABLE WIDTH=100% CELLPADDING=0 CELLSPACING=0 BORDER=0>
          <TR VALIGN=TOP>
          <TD WIDTH=2%><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>A.</B> </FONT> </TD>
          <TD WIDTH=98%><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>
        The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted
          accounting principles for U.S. mutual funds. The funds consistently follow such
          policies in preparing their financial statements. </FONT></TD>
          </TR>
          </TABLE>
          <BR>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 4-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<TABLE WIDTH=100% CELLPADDING=0 CELLSPACING=0 BORDER=0>
<TR VALIGN=TOP>
<TD WIDTH=2%>&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH=98%><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>1.</B> <B>Security
          Valuation: </B>Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York
          Stock Exchange (generally 4:00 p.m. Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity
          securities are valued at the latest quoted
sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each
security trades; such securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean
of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not
readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring
before the funds&#146; pricing time but after the close of the securities&#146; primary
markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair value.
Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&#146;s net asset
value. Temporary cash investments acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the
latest bid prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such
factors as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by
independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at amortized
cost, which approximates market value.</FONT></TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
<BR>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 4-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<TABLE WIDTH=100% CELLPADDING=0 CELLSPACING=0 BORDER=0>
<TR VALIGN=TOP>
<TD WIDTH=2%>&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH=98%><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>2.</B> <B>Futures Contracts: </B>The funds use index futures contracts to a limited
          extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market,
          enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. A
          fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the
          market, or sell futures contracts in response to cash outflows, thereby
          simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a
          cash balance for liquidity. A fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures
          contracts instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be
          priced more attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks
          associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between
          changes in market values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures
          contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market. Futures contracts are
          valued at their quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate principal amounts
          of the contracts are not recorded in the financial statements. Fluctuations in
          the value of the contracts are recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an
          asset (liability) and in the Statement of Operations as unrealized appreciation
          (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as
          realized futures gains (losses). </FONT></TD>
          </TR>
          </TABLE>
          <BR>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 4-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<TABLE WIDTH=100% CELLPADDING=0 CELLSPACING=0 BORDER=0>
<TR VALIGN=TOP>
<TD WIDTH=2%>&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH=98%><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>3.</B> <B>Federal Income Taxes: </B>Each fund intends to continue to qualify as a
          regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income.
          Accordingly, no provision for federal income taxes is required in the financial
          statements. </FONT></TD>
          </TR>
          </TABLE>
          <BR>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 4-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<TABLE WIDTH=100% CELLPADDING=0 CELLSPACING=0 BORDER=0>
<TR VALIGN=TOP>
<TD WIDTH=2%>&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH=98%><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>4.</B>
          <B>Distributions: </B>Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the
          ex-dividend date. </FONT></TD>
          </TR>
          </TABLE>
          <BR>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 4-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<TABLE WIDTH=100% CELLPADDING=0 CELLSPACING=0 BORDER=0>
<TR VALIGN=TOP>
<TD WIDTH=2%>&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH=98%><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>5.</B> <B>Security Lending: </B>The funds may lend their securities to qualified
          institutional borrowers to earn additional income. Security loans are required
          to be secured at all times by collateral at least equal to the market value of
          securities loaned. The funds invest cash collateral received in Vanguard Market
          Liquidity Fund, and record a liability for the return of the collateral, during
          the period the securities are on loan. Security lending income represents the
          income earned on investing cash collateral, less expenses associated with the
          loan. </FONT></TD>
          </TR>
          </TABLE>
          <BR>


<BR>

<P ALIGN=CENTER><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=1> 29</FONT></P>

<HR SIZE=5 COLOR=GRAY NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Sub 2 Left-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<h1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="1" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>NOTES
TO FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (CONTINUED)</B> </FONT> </h1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 4-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<TABLE WIDTH=100% CELLPADDING=0 CELLSPACING=0 BORDER=0>
<TR VALIGN=TOP>
<TD WIDTH=2%>&nbsp;</TD>
<TD WIDTH=98%><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>6.
          Other: </B>Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income
          includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and
          is accrued daily. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities
          are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale
          of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold. Each class
          of shares has equal rights as to assets and earnings, except that each class
          separately bears certain class-specific expenses related to maintenance of
          shareholder accounts (included in Management and Administrative expenses) and
          shareholder reporting. Marketing and distribution expenses are allocated to each
          class of shares based on a method approved by the board of trustees. Income,
          other non-class-specific expenses, and gains and losses on investments are
          allocated to each class of shares based on its relative net assets.</FONT></TD>
          </TR>
          </TABLE>

<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>As a shareholder of the fund, you
incur ongoing costs, which include costs for portfolio management, administrative
services, and shareholder reports (like this one), among others. Operating expenses, which
are deducted from a fund&#146;s gross income, directly reduce the investment return of the
fund. A fund&#146;s expenses are expressed as a percentage of its average net assets. This
figure is known as the expense ratio. The following examples are intended to help you
understand the ongoing costs (in dollars) of investing in your fund and to compare these
costs with those of other mutual funds. The examples are based on an investment of $1,000
made at the beginning of the period shown and held for the entire period. <br><br>The table below
illustrates your fund&#146;s costs in two ways: <br><br><B>&#149;</B> <B>Based on actual fund
return. </B>This section helps you to estimate the actual expenses that you paid over the
period. The &#147;Ending Account Value&#148; shown is derived from the fund&#146;s actual
return, and the third column shows the dollar amount that would have been paid by an
investor who started with $1,000 in the fund. You may use the information here, together
with the amount you invested, to estimate the expenses that you paid over the period. </FONT></P>

Paid During Period.&#148; </FONT></P>

<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>TRUSTEES RENEW ADVISORY
ARRANGEMENT </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The board of trustees of Vanguard
Extended Market Index Fund and Mid-Cap Index Fund has renewed the funds&#146; investment
advisory arrangement with The Vanguard Group, Inc. Vanguard&#151;through its Quantitative
Equity Group&#151;serves as the investment advisor for the funds. The board determined
that continuing the funds&#146; internalized management structure was in the best
interests of the funds and their shareholders. <br><br>The board based its decision upon its most
recent evaluation of the advisor&#146;s investment staff, portfolio management process,
and performance. The trustees considered the factors discussed below, among others.
However, no single factor determined whether the board approved the arrangement. Rather,
it was the totality of the circumstances that drove the board&#146;s decision. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="1" COLOR="#FF00FF">NATURE, EXTENT, AND
QUALITY OF SERVICES </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The board considered the quality of
the funds&#146; investment management over both short-and long-term periods, and took into
account the organizational depth and stability of the advisor. Vanguard has been managing
investments for more than two decades. George U. Sauter, Vanguard managing director and
chief investment officer, has been in the investment management business since 1985 and
oversees more than $600 billion in assets (stocks and bonds). Mr. Sauter has led the
Quantitative Equity Group since 1987. The Quantitative Equity Group adheres to a sound,
disciplined investment management process; the team has considerable experience,
stability, and depth. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The board concluded that
Vanguard&#146;s experience, stability, depth, and performance, among other factors,
warranted continuation of the advisory arrangement. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="1" COLOR="#FF00FF">INVESTMENT PERFORMANCE </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The board considered the short- and
long-term performance of the funds, including any periods of outperformance or
underperformance of relevant benchmarks and peer groups. The board noted that the funds
have performed in line with expectations, and that their results have been consistent with
their investment strategies. Information about the funds&#146; performance, including some
of the data considered by the board, can be found in the &#147;Performance Summaries&#148;
section of this report. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="1" COLOR="#FF00FF">COST </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The funds&#146; expense ratios were
far below the average expense ratio charged by funds in their respective peer groups. The
funds&#146; advisory expense ratios were also well below their peer-group averages.
Information about the funds&#146; expense ratios appears in the &#147;About Your
Fund&#146;s Expenses&#148; section of this report as well as in the &#147;Financial
Statements&#148; section. <br><br>The board does not conduct a profitability analysis of Vanguard
because of Vanguard&#146;s unique &#147;at-cost&#148; structure. Unlike most other mutual
fund management companies, Vanguard is owned by the funds it oversees, and produces
&#147;profits&#148; only in the form of reduced expenses for fund shareholders. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="1" COLOR="#FF00FF">THE BENEFIT OF ECONOMIES
OF SCALE </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The board of trustees concluded that
the funds&#146; low-cost arrangement with Vanguard ensures that the funds will realize
economies of scale as they grow, with the cost to shareholders declining as fund assets
increase. <br><br>The board will consider whether to renew the advisory arrangement again after a
one-year period. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="1" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>STATEMENT OF NET
ASSETS&#151;INVESTMENTS SUMMARY (UNAUDITED)</B> </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>This Statement summarizes the
fund&#146;s holdings by asset type (common stocks, bonds, etc.) and by industry sector.
Details are reported for each of the fund&#146;s 50 largest individual holdings and for
investments that, in total for any issuer, represent more than 1% of the fund&#146;s net
assets. The total value of smaller holdings is reported as a single amount within each
category. Other assets are added to, and liabilities are subtracted from, the value of
<I>Total Investments </I>to calculate the fund&#146;s <I>Net Assets</I>. Finally, <I>Net
Assets </I>are divided by the outstanding shares of the fund to arrive at its share price,
or <I>Net Asset Value (NAV) Per Share</I>. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>At the end of the Statement, you will
find a table displaying the composition of the fund&#146;s net assets. Because all income
and any realized gains must be distributed to shareholders each year, the bulk of net
assets consists of <I>Paid-in Capital </I>(money invested by shareholders). The amounts
shown for <I>Undistributed Net Investment Income </I>and <I>Accumulated Net Realized Gains
</I>usually approximate the sums the fund had available to distribute to shareholders as
income dividends or capital gains as of the statement date, but may differ because certain
investments or transactions may be treated differently for financial statement and tax
purposes. Any <I>Accumulated Net Realized Losses</I>, and any cumulative excess of
distributions over net income or net realized gains, will appear as negative balances.
<I>Unrealized Appreciation (Depreciation) </I>is the difference between the market value
of the fund&#146;s investments and their cost, and reflects the gains (losses) that would
be realized if the fund were to sell all of its investments at their statement-date
values. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The fund provides a complete list of
its holdings four times in each fiscal year, at the quarter-ends. For the second and
fourth fiscal quarters, the complete listing of the fund&#146;s holdings is available
electronically on Vanguard.com and on the Securities and Exchange Commission&#146;s
website (www.sec.gov), or you can have it mailed to you without charge by calling
800-662-7447. For the first and third fiscal quarters, the fund files the lists with the
SEC on Form N-Q. Shareholders can look up the fund&#146;s Forms N-Q on the SEC&#146;s
website; Forms N-Q may also be reviewed and copied at the SEC&#146;s Public Reference Room
(see the back cover of the accompanying report for further information). </FONT></P>

<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>CHAIRMAN'S LETTER</FONT></H1>

<IMG SRC="picturebrennan.gif" ALIGN="LEFT" TITLE="Picture of John J. Brennan" ALT="Picture of John J. Brennan">

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Left-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="Fuchsia">Dear Shareholder,</FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="Fuchsia">U.S. stock prices finished the first
half of 2005 mostly flat, as the market&#146;s           weak spots subsumed its pockets
of strength. The stocks of energy-related           companies&#151;beneficiaries of
persistently high oil prices&#151;were among the           strongest performers, while
technology and consumer discretionary stocks           struggled. </FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The four Vanguard large-capitalization
index funds captured the returns of their target benchmarks, in most cases trailing by
slim margins consistent with the funds&#146; costs. The Value Index Fund produced the
highest six-month returns, the Growth Index Fund the lowest. The returns of the Large-Cap
Index and Total Stock Market Index Funds were in-between. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The table on page 2 presents the total
returns of the funds and their target indexes, as well as the average returns of their
peer groups. The funds&#146; starting and ending net asset values, as well as their income
distributions, appear in a table on page 6. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>During the half-year, the Total Stock
Market Index Fund switched its benchmark from the Dow Jones Wilshire 5000 Composite Index
to the Morgan Stanley Capital International&reg; (MSCI&reg;) US Broad Market Index,
another measure of the broad U.S. stock market. The new benchmark incorporates many of
Vanguard&#146;s views of best practices in index construction, including: </FONT></P>



<TABLE CELLPADDING="7" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR VALIGN=Bottom>
     <TD WIDTH="2%" ALIGN="LEFT" VALIGN="TOP"><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></TD>
     <TD WIDTH="98%" ALIGN="LEFT"><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Market weightings based on stocks&#146; &#147;float&#148;&#151;those shares that are readily available to the public.</FONT></TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN=Bottom>
     <TD ALIGN="LEFT" VALIGN="TOP"><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></TD>
     <TD ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Inclusion of companies incorporated in the United States, as well as internationally based companies with equity trading activity, shareholders, and operations predominantly in the United States.</FONT></TD></TR>
<TR VALIGN=Bottom>
     <TD ALIGN="LEFT" VALIGN="TOP"><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></TD>
     <TD ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Exclusion of limited partnerships.</FONT></TD></TR>
</TABLE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Left-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="Fuchsia">STOCKS MADE LITTLE HEADWAY </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Following a formidable rally to close
out 2004, U.S. stocks at different times stumbled and surged during the first half of
2005, but the net effect was a flat finish for the broad market. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Investors were cheered as home-buying
activity remained high by historical standards, knowing that new homeowners fuel the
economy by buying appliances and other home furnishings. But the market also faced
headwinds: rising short-term interest rates and gas prices (which can curtail consumer
spending), and mounting trade and budget deficits. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Value stocks&#151;those with low
prices relative to corporate earnings, book value, and other measures&#151;extended their
five-year winning streak over growth stocks, which dominated the market in the late 1990s.
In a reversal of recent trends, returns for large-cap stocks topped those of the
market&#146;s smaller companies. International stocks outperformed their U.S.
counterparts; however, a strengthening dollar wiped out most of that edge for U.S.
investors. </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN=CENTER><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>2</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="page-break-after:always"></P>
<!-- MARKER PAGE="sheet: 5; page: 5" -->

<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>A lower-cost class of shares available
to many longtime shareholders and to those with significant investments in the fund. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2"><B>Institutional Shares</B> </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>This class of shares also carries low
expenses and is available for a minimum investment of $5 million. </FONT></P>

<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2"><B>VIPER&reg; Shares</B> </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Traded on the American Stock Exchange,  VIPERs&reg; (U.S.  Pat. No.  6,879,964 B2) are available only through  brokers.  The table on page 2 shows VIPER returns based on both the AMEX market price and the
net asset value for a share.</FONT></P>

<BR>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Left-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="Fuchsia">THE BOND MARKET&#146;S DICHOTOMY PERSISTED </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The Lehman Brothers Aggregate Bond Index, which reflects the taxable investment-grade bond market, posted a 2.5% return during the six months. U.S. government and municipal issues performed best.
Corporate securities matched the index return, and mortgage-backed debt trailed.</FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The Federal Reserve Board raised its target
for the federal funds rate in four equal steps to 3.25%. The yield of the 3-month U.S.
Treasury bill moved in sync, closing the period at 3.12%. Long-term rates didn&#146;t
follow. The yield of the 10-year Treasury note finished the period at 3.91%, a drop of 31
basis points (0.31 percentage point) over the six months. The yield of the 30-year
Treasury bond fell 64 basis points to 4.19%. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Left-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="Fuchsia">ENERGY STOCKS RALLIED, WHILE TECH SHARES STRUGGLED</FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The broad stock market&#146;s flat
performance masked significant variation among different market segments. Energy-related
stocks, for example, registered solid double-digit gains, as fuel prices continued to
hover at unprecedented heights. Health care stocks were another pocket of strength,
bolstered by excellent returns from the stocks of HMOs and other health-insurance
providers. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>These gains were offset by weak
showings from technology, consumer discretionary and, to a lesser extent, auto &amp;
transportation stocks. The technology sector was buffeted by high-profile earnings
disappointments, while consumer discretionary stocks retreated on weakness in select
retailers. The relatively small auto &amp; transportation sector was hit hard by the

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The performances of the four Vanguard
large-cap index funds were largely a function of their exposures to these different
industry groups. The Value Index Fund produced the highest returns (+1.3% for Investor
Shares), reflecting its relatively heavy weightings in the integrated oils and utilities
sectors and its modest stakes in technology and consumer discretionary stocks. This
positioning was inverted in the Growth Index Fund, which registered the lowest returns
(&#150;1.5% for Investor Shares). The Growth Index Fund&#146;s losses in the technology
and consumer discretionary sectors were somewhat offset by the fund&#146;s sizable stake
in the solidly performing health care sector. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The returns of the Large-Cap Index and
the Total Stock Market Index Funds reflected the blended performances of the Growth and
Value Index Funds. The Investor Shares of the Large-Cap Index Fund returned &#150;0.1%,
and those of the Total Stock Market Index Fund returned &#150;0.3%, reflecting the broader
index&#146;s exposure to poorly performing small-cap stocks, a market laggard during the
half-year. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>All four index funds closely tracked
the returns of their benchmarks. Such precision is a product of the proprietary-trading
and portfolio-construction methodologies developed by Vanguard Quantitative </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="Fuchsia">TIMELESS ADVICE FOR NOW </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The markets and the news media tend to
focus on what to do <I>now</I>. As we never get tired of reminding our clients, successful
long-term investing doesn&#146;t mean paying attention to yesterday&#146;s performance,
today&#146;s news, or predictions for tomorrow. Instead, reaching your long-term goals
requires a more patient approach&#151;an approach that the Vanguard large-cap index funds
are ideally suited to support. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Whether the stock market rises or
falls sharply or as in the past six months, meanders sideways, the low-cost broadly
diversified large-cap index funds can give you exposure to the entire U.S. stock market or
to significant segments, positioning you to benefit from the U.S. economy&#146;s long-term
growth potential. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Long-term success is much more likely
when you ignore the daily noise of the marketplace and maintain a steady, diversified mix
of low-cost stock, bond, and short-term investments tailored to your circumstances. I hope
you take advantage of our website, Vanguard.com, where you&#146;ll find extensive
information and useful tools to help you apply these principles to your own portfolio. </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2"><B>GLOSSARY OF INVESTMENT TERMS</B> </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Beta.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">A measure of the magnitude of a fund&#146;s past share-price fluctuations in
relation to the ups and downs of a given market index. The index is assigned a
beta of 1.00. Compared with a given index, a fund with a beta of 1.20 typically
would have seen its share price rise or fall by 12% when the index rose or fell
by 10%. A fund&#146;s beta should be reviewed in conjunction with its R-squared
(see definition below). The lower the R-squared, the less correlation there is
between the fund and the index, and the less reliable beta is as an indicator of
volatility. </FONT></P>

<HR NOSHADE COLOR=#000000 SIZE=1>
<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Earnings Growth Rate.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The
average annual rate of growth in earnings over the past five years for the stocks now in a
fund. </FONT> </P>
<HR NOSHADE COLOR=#000000 SIZE=1>
<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Expense Ratio.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The percentage
of a fund&#146;s average net assets used to pay its annual administrative and advisory
expenses. These expenses directly reduce returns to investors. </FONT> </P>
<HR NOSHADE COLOR=#000000 SIZE=1>
<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Foreign Holdings.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The
percentage of a fund&#146;s equity assets represented by stocks or depositary receipts of
companies based outside the United States. </FONT> </P>
<HR NOSHADE COLOR=#000000 SIZE=1>
<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Median Market Cap.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">An indicator
of the size of companies in which a fund invests; the midpoint of market capitalization
(market price x shares outstanding) of a fund&#146;s stocks, weighted by the proportion of
the fund&#146;s assets invested in each stock. Stocks representing half of the fund&#146;s
assets have market capitalizations above the median, and the rest are below it. </FONT> </P>
<HR NOSHADE COLOR=#000000 SIZE=1>
<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Price/Book Ratio.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The share
price of a stock divided by its net worth, or book value, per share. For a fund, the
weighted average price/book ratio of the stocks it holds. </FONT> </P>
<HR NOSHADE COLOR=#000000 SIZE=1>
<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Price/Earnings Ratio.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The ratio
of a stock&#146;s current price to its per-share earnings over the past year. For a fund,
the weighted average P/E of the stocks it holds. P/E is an indicator of market
expectations about corporate prospects; the higher the P/E, the greater the expectations
for a company&#146;s future growth. </FONT> </P>
<HR NOSHADE COLOR=#000000 SIZE=1>
<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>R-Squared.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">A measure of how much of a fund&#146;s past returns can be explained by the
returns from the market in general, as measured by a given index. If a
fund&#146;s total returns were precisely synchronized with an index&#146;s
returns, its R-squared would be 1.00. If the fund&#146;s returns bore no
relationship to the index&#146;s returns, its R-squared would be 0. </FONT></P>

<HR NOSHADE COLOR=#000000 SIZE=1>
<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Return on Equity.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The annual
average rate of return generated by a company during the past five years for each dollar
of shareholder&#146;s equity (net income divided by shareholder&#146;s equity). For a
fund, the weighted average return on equity for the companies whose stocks it holds. </FONT> </P>
<HR NOSHADE COLOR=#000000 SIZE=1>
<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Short-Term Reserves.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The
percentage of a fund invested in highly liquid, short-term securities that can be readily
converted to cash. </FONT> </P>
<HR NOSHADE COLOR=#000000 SIZE=1>
<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Turnover Rate.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">An indication of
the fund&#146;s trading activity. Funds with high turnover rates incur higher transaction
costs and may be more likely to distribute capital gains (which may be taxable to
investors). The turnover rate excludes in-kind transactions, which have minimal impact on
costs. </FONT> </P>
<HR NOSHADE COLOR=#000000 SIZE=1>
<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>Yield.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">A snapshot of a fund&#146;s income from interest and dividends. The yield,
expressed as a percentage of the fund&#146;s net asset value, is based on income
earned over the past 30 days and is annualized, or projected forward for the
coming year. The index yield is based on the current annualized rate of income
provided by securities in the index. </FONT></P>
<HR NOSHADE COLOR=#000000 SIZE=1>

<P ALIGN=CENTER><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>12</FONT></P>
<P STYLE="page-break-after:always"></P>
<!-- MARKER PAGE="sheet: 15; page: 15" -->
<HR SIZE=5 COLOR=GRAY NOSHADE>





<TABLE WIDTH="100%" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0">
<TR VALIGN="Middle">
     <TD WIDTH="20%" ALIGN="Center" VALIGN="Middle"><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2"><B>As of 6/30/2005</B> </FONT></TD>
     <TD WIDTH="80%"><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2"><B>PERFORMANCE SUMMARIES<BR><BR>
All of the returns in this report
represent past performance, which is not a guarantee of future results that may be
achieved by the funds. (For performance data current to the most recent month-end, which
may be higher or lower than that cited, visit our website at www.vanguard.com.) Note, too,
that both investment returns and principal value can fluctuate widely, so an
investor&#146;s shares, when sold, could be worth more or less than their original cost.
</B>The returns shown do not reflect taxes that a shareholder would pay on fund
distributions or on the sale of fund shares. </FONT></TD></TR>
</TABLE>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Left-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2"><B>GROWTH INDEX FUND</B></FONT></P>

<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="Fuchsia">STATEMENT OF NET ASSETS </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The Statements of Net Assets&#151;an
integral part of the Financial Statements for Vanguard Total Stock Market Index Fund and
Large-Cap Index Fund&#151;are included as inserts to this report. The Growth Index and
Value Index Funds&#146; Statements of Net Assets are provided below. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>This Statement provides a detailed
list of each fund&#146;s holdings, including each security&#146;s market value on the last
day of the reporting period. Securities are grouped and subtotaled by asset type (common
stocks, bonds, etc.) and by industry sector. Other assets are added to, and liabilities
are subtracted from, the value of <I>Total Investments </I>to calculate the fund&#146;s
<I>Net Assets</I>. Finally, <I>Net Assets </I>are divided by the outstanding shares of the
fund to arrive at its share price, or <I>Net Asset Value (NAV) Per Share</I>. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>At the end of the Statement of Net
Assets, you will find a table displaying the composition of the fund&#146;s net assets.
Because all income and any realized gains must be distributed to shareholders each year,
the bulk of net assets consists of <I>Paid-in Capital </I>(money invested by
shareholders). The amounts shown for <I>Undistributed Net Investment Income </I>and
<I>Accumulated Net Realized Gains </I>usually approximate the sums the fund had available
to distribute to shareholders as income dividends or capital gains as of the statement
date, but may differ because certain investments or transactions may be treated
differently for financial statement and tax purposes. Any <I>Accumulated Net Realized
Losses</I>, and any cumulative excess of distributions over net income or net realized
gains, will appear as negative balances. <I>Unrealized Appreciation (Depreciation) </I>is
the difference between the market value of the fund&#146;s investments and their cost, and
reflects the gains (losses) that would be realized if the fund were to sell all of its
investments at their statement-date values. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Each fund provides a complete list of
its holdings four times in each fiscal year, at the quarter-ends. For the second and
fourth fiscal quarters, the lists appear in the fund&#146;s semiannual and annual reports
to shareholders. For the first and third fiscal quarters, the fund files the lists with
the Securities and Exchange Commission on Form N-Q. Shareholders can look up the
fund&#146;s Forms N-Q on the SEC&#146;s website at www.sec.gov. Forms N-Q may also be
reviewed and copied at the SEC&#146;s Public Reference Room (see the back cover of this
report for further information). </FONT></P>

<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>This table summarizes each fund&#146;s
investment results and distributions to shareholders on a per-share basis for each class
of shares. It also presents the <I>Total Return </I>and shows net investment income and
expenses as percentages of average net assets. These data will help you assess: the
variability of the fund&#146;s net income and total returns from year to year; the
relative contributions of net income and capital gains to the fund&#146;s total return;
how much it costs to operate the fund; and the extent to which the fund tends to
distribute capital gains. The table also shows the <I>Portfolio Turnover Rate</I>, a
measure of trading activity. A turnover rate of 100% means that the average security is
held in the fund for one year. </FONT></P>

<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="Fuchsia">NOTES TO FINANCIAL STATEMENTS </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Vanguard Growth Index, Value Index, Large-Cap
Index, and Total Stock Market Index Funds are registered under the Investment Company Act
of 1940 as open-end investment companies, or mutual funds. The funds offer four classes of
shares: Investor Shares, Admiral Shares, Institutional Shares, and VIPER Shares. Investor
Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#146;s minimum purchase
requirements. Admiral Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative,
servicing, tenure, and account-size criteria. Institutional Shares are designed for
investors who meet certain administrative and servicing criteria and invest a minimum of
$5 million. VIPER Shares are listed for trading on the American Stock Exchange; they can
be purchased and sold through a broker. The Large-Cap Index Fund Institutional Shares were
first issued on June 30, 2005. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>A.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted
accounting principles for U.S. mutual funds. The funds consistently follow such
policies in preparing their financial statements. </FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Hang Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<TABLE WIDTH=100% CELLPADDING=0 CELLSPACING=0 BORDER=0>
<TR VALIGN=TOP>
<TD WIDTH=2%><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>1. </B></FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH=98%><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Security Valuation:</B> Securities are valued as of the close of trading on           the New York
Stock Exchange (generally 4:00 p.m. Eastern time) on the valuation           date. Equity
securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official           closing
prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such
          securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the
latest           quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are
not           readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events
          occurring before the funds&#146; pricing time but after the close of the
          securities&#146; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of
          trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund
          are valued at that fund&#146;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments
          acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the latest bid prices or
          using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as
          security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by
          independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at
          amortized cost, which approximates market value.</FONT></TD>

</TR>
</TABLE>
<BR>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Hang Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<TABLE WIDTH=100% CELLPADDING=0 CELLSPACING=0 BORDER=0>
<TR VALIGN=TOP>
<TD WIDTH=2%><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>2.</B> </FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH=98%><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Futures
Contracts: </B>The funds use index futures contracts to a limited           extent, with
the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market,           enhancing
returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The           funds may
purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the           market,
or sell futures contracts in response to cash outflows, thereby           simulating a
fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a           cash
balance for liquidity. The funds may seek to enhance returns by using           futures
contracts instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed           to be
priced more attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks
          associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between
          changes in market values of stocks held by the funds and the prices of futures
          contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market.</FONT></TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
<BR>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Hang Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<TABLE WIDTH=100% CELLPADDING=0 CELLSPACING=0 BORDER=0>
<TR VALIGN=TOP>
<TD WIDTH=2%><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2></FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH=98%><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Futures contracts
are valued at their quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate principal amounts of
the contracts are not recorded in the financial statements. Fluctuations in the value of
the contracts are recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in
the Statement of Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts
are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses). </FONT></TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
<BR>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Hang Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<TABLE WIDTH=100% CELLPADDING=0 CELLSPACING=0 BORDER=0>
<TR VALIGN=TOP>
<TD WIDTH=2%><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>3.</B> </FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH=98%><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Federal
Income Taxes: </B>Each fund intends to continue to qualify as a           regulated
investment company and distribute all of its taxable income.           Accordingly, no
provision for federal income taxes is required in the financial           statements.</FONT></TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
<BR>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Hang Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<TABLE WIDTH=100% CELLPADDING=0 CELLSPACING=0 BORDER=0>
<TR VALIGN=TOP>
<TD WIDTH=2%><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>4.</B></FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH=98%><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Distributions:
</B>Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the           ex-dividend date.</FONT></TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
<BR>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Hang Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<TABLE WIDTH=100% CELLPADDING=0 CELLSPACING=0 BORDER=0>
<TR VALIGN=TOP>
<TD WIDTH=2%><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>5. </B></FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH=98%><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Security
Lending: </B>The funds may lend their securities to qualified           institutional
borrowers to earn additional income. Security loans are required           to be secured
at all times by collateral at least equal to the market value of           securities
loaned. The funds invest cash collateral received in Vanguard Market           Liquidity
Fund, and record a liability for the return of the collateral, during           the
period the securities are on loan. Security lending income represents the
          income earned on investing cash collateral, less expenses associated with the
          loan.</FONT></TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
<BR>


<P ALIGN=CENTER><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>49</FONT></P>

<P ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="1" COLOR="Fuchsia">NOTES TO FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (CONTINUED)</FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Hang Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<TABLE WIDTH=100% CELLPADDING=0 CELLSPACING=0 BORDER=0>
<TR VALIGN=TOP>
<TD WIDTH=2%><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>6.</B></FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH=98%><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2"><B>Other: </B>Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income
includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and
is accrued daily. Security transactions are accounted for on the date
securities are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses)
on the sale of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold. </FONT></TD>
</TR>

<TD WIDTH=98%><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Each class
of shares has equal rights as to assets and earnings, except that each class separately
bears certain class-specific expenses related to maintenance of shareholder accounts
(included in Management and Administrative expenses) and shareholder reporting. Marketing
and distribution expenses are allocated to each class of shares based on a method
approved by the board of trustees. Income, other non-class-specific expenses, and gains
and losses on investments are allocated to each class of shares based on its relative net
assets. </FONT></TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>

<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF"><B>C.</B> </FONT> <FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">Distributions
are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment income and
realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes. Differences may be
permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are reclassified among capital
accounts in the financial statements to reflect their tax character. Temporary
differences arise when certain items of income, expense, gain, or loss are
recognized in different periods for financial statement and tax purposes; these
differences will reverse at some time in the future. Differences in
classification may also result from the treatment of short-term gains as
ordinary income for tax purposes. </FONT> </P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>During the six months ended June 30,
2005, the Growth Index, Value Index, Large-Cap Index, and Total Stock Market Index Funds
realized $4,667,000, $13,728,000, $858,000, and $34,895,000, respectively, of net capital
gains resulting from in-kind redemptions&#151;in which shareholders exchanged fund shares
for securities held by the fund rather than for cash. Because such gains are not taxable
to the funds, and are not distributed to shareholders, they have been reclassified from
accumulated net realized gains to paid-in capital. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>As a shareholder of the fund, you
incur ongoing costs, which include costs for portfolio management, administrative
services, and shareholder reports (like this one), among others. Operating expenses, which
are deducted from a fund&#146;s gross income, directly reduce the investment return of the
fund. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>A fund&#146;s expenses are expressed
as a percentage of its average net assets. This figure is known as the expense ratio. The
following examples are intended to help you understand the ongoing costs (in dollars) of
investing in your fund and to compare these costs with those of other mutual funds. The
examples are based on an investment of $1,000 made at the beginning of the period shown
and held for the entire period. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The table at left and on page 56
illustrates your fund&#146;s costs in two ways: </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2"><B>TRUSTEES RENEW ADVISORY ARRANGEMENT</B> </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The board of trustees of Vanguard
Growth Index Fund, Value Index Fund, Large-Cap Index Fund, and Total Stock Market Index
Fund has renewed the funds&#146; investment advisory arrangement with The Vanguard Group,
Inc. Vanguard&#151;through its Quantitative Equity Group&#151;serves as the investment
advisor for the funds. The board determined that continuing the funds&#146; internalized
management structure was in the best interests of the funds and their shareholders. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The board based its decision upon its
most recent evaluation of the advisor&#146;s investment staff, portfolio management
process, and performance. The trustees considered the factors discussed below, among
others. However, no single factor determined whether the board approved the arrangement.
Rather, it was the totality of the circumstances that drove the board&#146;s decision. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF">NATURE, EXTENT, AND QUALITY OF SERVICES </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The board considered the quality of
the funds&#146; investment management over both short-and long-term periods, and took into
account the organizational depth and stability of the advisor. Vanguard has been managing
investments for more than two decades. George U. Sauter, Vanguard managing director and
chief investment officer, has been in the investment management business since 1985 and
oversees more than $600 billion in assets (stocks and bonds). Mr. Sauter has led the
Quantitative Equity Group since 1987. The Quantitative Equity Group adheres to a sound,
disciplined investment management process; the team has considerable experience,
stability, and depth. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The board concluded that
Vanguard&#146;s experience, stability, depth, and performance, among other factors,
warranted continuation of the advisory arrangement. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF">INVESTMENT PERFORMANCE </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The board considered the short- and
long-term performance of the funds, including any periods of outperformance or
underperformance of relevant benchmarks and their peer groups. The board noted that the
funds have performed in line with expectations, and that their results have been
consistent with their investment strategies. Information about the funds&#146;
performance, including some of the data considered by the board, can be found in the
&#147;Performance Summaries&#148; section of this report. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF">COST </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The funds&#146; expense ratios were
far below the average expense ratios charged by funds in their respective peer groups. The
funds&#146; advisory expense ratios were also well below their peer-group averages.
Information about the funds&#146; expense ratios appears in the &#147;About Your
Fund&#146;s Expenses&#148; section of this report as well as in the &#147;Financial
Statements&#148; section.<BR><BR>The board does not conduct a profitability analysis of Vanguard
because of Vanguard&#146;s unique &#147;at-cost&#148; structure. Unlike most other mutual
fund management companies, Vanguard is owned by the funds it oversees, and produces
&#147;profits&#148; only in the form of reduced expenses for fund shareholders. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF00FF">THE BENEFIT OF ECONOMIES OF SCALE </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The board of trustees concluded that
the funds&#146; low-cost arrangement with Vanguard ensures that the funds will realize
economies of scale as they grow, with the cost to shareholders declining as fund assets
increase. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The board will consider whether to
renew the advisory arrangement again after a one-year period. </FONT></P>
